step1_summary: Symptoms: Tight chest (3 hours), slight shortness of breath, wheezy, cough (consistent, worse at night), had a cold last week, no productive cough.
Past medical history: Asthma, hay fever, skin allergies, past hospitalization for asthma, eczema and milk protein allergy as a child.
Medications/allergies: Ventolin (Salbutamol) inhaler, Clenil (steroid) inhaler, no drug allergies.
Family/social history: Family history of asthma (father) and eczema (mother).

I: Viral upper respiratory infection: Recent history of cold, runny nose, sore throat and cough suggest a lingering viral infection.
Asthma exacerbation: History of asthma, wheezing, tight chest, and shortness of breath are consistent with asthma.
A: Allergic asthma or rhinitis: Known allergies to dust and family history of allergies may be contributing to symptoms.

supporting_evidence: History of asthma, not using Ventolin or Clenil recently.
Wheezing and shortness of breath, especially on exertion.
opposing_evidence: No significant opposition evidence present; symptoms align well with asthma exacerbation.
